sections.heading: The Stain Is Here. The Leak Is Somewhere Else.
body: A week of rain, and the brown ring on the ceiling is bigger than it was Tuesday. The roof came with the house, so you wonder if the whole thing is going. You dread two calls: the roofer who says "whole new roof, sign today," and the one who never calls back.

You just want someone to get up there and tell you the truth. Water doesn't drip where it gets in. It runs along the decking first, so the stain can sit feet from the real opening, and nobody can read that from the driveway.

sections.heading: Find It First. Check It After.
body: Plenty of roofers look at a ceiling stain and quote a new roof. It's the bigger ticket, and nobody has to crawl through a hot attic to sell it.
If the water was really coming in at a chimney or a pipe boot, you've paid for a roof and you still have the leak.
We go in order. Anthony gets into the attic and up on the roof until he knows where the water is coming from. Sometimes it isn't the roof at all, and then you hear that too.
Then you get a detailed estimate for what's really wrong, so the price is for your roof and not for one nobody looked at.

sections.heading: What Your Roof Is Telling You
body: Most roof calls start with something you can see. Here's what usually causes it, and what we do about it.

items.title: A stain on the ceiling after a rain
items.text: Water runs along the decking and down a rafter before it drips, so the stain is often several feet from the opening. We start in the attic, follow the trail up to the roof, and fix where the water gets in, which isn't always the shingles.

items.title: Shingles in the yard after a wind storm
items.text: Wind breaks the seal strip under a shingle, then peels it off the next time it blows, and the felt underneath soaks up every rain after that. We replace what's missing and check the shingles around it, because a broken seal can look fine from the ground.

items.title: A drip near the chimney or a plumbing pipe
items.text: Flashing around chimneys pulls loose, and the rubber boots around pipes crack in the sun years before the shingles wear out. Either one is a small repair that costs a fraction of a roof, once someone finds it.

items.title: Curling shingles and grit in the gutters
items.text: Sun, wind and hail have worn the granules off, and the shingles underneath are giving out across the slope. Patches only buy a season at that point, so we write a detailed estimate for a new roof in composition shingles, metal or tile.

sections.quote: We found a leak in our roof. River City handled it all very professionally and in a timely manner. I would definitely recommend them for any of your roofing needs.
sections.name: Lindsey F.

sections.heading: Roof Replacement
body: Asphalt shingles wear out from the sun first, then from Kansas wind and hail. Once the granules are gone, every repair only buys a season or two.
When a roof is at the end of its life, replacement is the job we put first. The old roof comes off to the decking, and a new one goes on in composition shingles, metal or tile.
We confirm you need one before we quote. The detailed estimate comes after we've seen your roof, so it's built for your house and not for an average one.

sections.heading: Roof Repair
body: Most leaks aren't a worn-out roof. They're one failed spot, and every rain after it opens soaks a little more of the decking, the insulation and the ceiling.
We fix everything from a minor leak to storm damage. Finding the real cause costs far less than the water damage that follows when it's ignored.

sections.heading: Roofing and Exterior Services
sections.intro: The roof edge, the gutters and the siding all meet, and water that gets past one shows up at the next. So one call covers the roof and the rest of the outside of the house.

items.q: Will my insurance pay for it?
items.a: It depends on your policy, your deductible and what caused the damage. Wind and hail are the usual claims. Check your policy for a separate wind and hail deductible, take dated photos, and keep receipts for temporary fixes. Anthony has talked to an insurance agent and filled out forms for a customer. We can't promise what your insurer will do.
Yes. We're local and family owned, at 3750 N Topeka St in Wichita, and customers deal with Anthony. Call (316) 295-2159 or stop by during office hours.

items.q: How do I know if I need a repair or a new roof?
items.a: We find out first. Anthony goes into the attic and up on the roof before any price is written. As a rule, one failed spot, like a flashing or a vent boot, is a repair. Curling, bare patches and granules in the gutters across the whole slope means the roof is at the end of its life. If you've already repaired it more than once, a new roof usually costs less than the third repair and the water damage between them.
Usually Anthony, the name you'll see in most of our reviews. He looks at the roof and answers calls and texts. You don't get handed from a salesperson to a stranger.
Yes. Call (316) 295-2159 and tell us what the roof is doing. We set a time to look at it, and the detailed estimate you get afterward costs you nothing.

items.q: What decides the price of a new roof?
items.a: Size and pitch come first, then the material you pick and how much old decking needs replacing once the old roof is off. Extra layers, chimneys, skylights and valleys add labor. That's why we write a detailed estimate after we've seen the roof, rather than quoting a per-square-foot number over the phone.
We're based on N Topeka St and work in Wichita. Call (316) 295-2159 with your address and we'll tell you.

sections.heading: Is It Time, or Is It a Repair?
body: Walk the yard and look up. Shingles curling at the edges, bare patches where the surface has worn away, and shingle grit washing out of your downspouts all say the same thing: the roof is worn out, not just damaged.
A roof like that can be patched, but the patch buys you a season, not a decade. If the whole slope is going, the money is better spent on the roof itself.

The opposite is just as true. One failed flashing or a bad vent boot is a [roof repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/), and replacing a sound roof because a stain showed up is money you didn't have to spend.
That's why we look before we quote: in the attic and on the roof, not from the driveway. Our job is to tell you which one you have.

sections.heading: Where the Roof Meets the Rest of the House
body: A new roof sits on top of the gutters, the fascia and the walls. If the edge is rotted or the gutters are pulling away, the best shingles in the world won't keep that water out of the house.

While the old roof is off, we can see these edges better than we ever will from the ground. Because we also do siding, gutters, paint and windows, we can tell you what we found and handle it ourselves instead of sending you to another company.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a New Roof
body: Call (316) 295-2159 and tell us how old the roof is and what you're seeing. We set a time to come out.
Someone from River City goes up on the roof, and into the attic if there's a leak, to see whether the roof is worn out or just damaged in one place.
Then you get a detailed estimate for whichever one it is. If it's a new roof, the estimate covers the material you choose and what has to come off first.

sections.heading: What Comes Off Before Anything Goes On
body: Replacement means more than new shingles. The old roof comes down to the decking, and that's where the real condition of the house shows.

Decking that's soft, stained or rotted from years of slow leaks gets replaced, not shingled over. New shingles nailed into bad wood loosen and fail early, and no one can see it once the roof is finished.

Underneath the shingles go the parts you'll never look at again: the underlayment, the flashing at the chimney, walls and valleys, and the vents that let the attic breathe. Reusing old flashing is how a brand-new roof ends up with an old leak.
Ventilation matters more than most people expect. A hot, wet attic cooks shingles from underneath and shortens the life of the roof you just bought.

sections.heading: Choosing the Material
body: We install composition shingles, metal roofing and tile. They are different roofs for different priorities.

**Composition shingles** are what most Wichita homes wear. They cost the least up front, come in plenty of colors, and any roofer in town can repair them. Asphalt shingles generally last 20 to 30 years, less on a hot slope or after hail.
**Metal** costs more to install and lasts considerably longer. It sheds snow and rain quickly and holds up well in wind. It's also louder in a downpour unless the roof is built with that in mind.
**Tile** is heavy and long-lived. The roof framing has to be able to carry it, so it's a decision to settle before anyone orders material, not after.

Kansas weather decides some of this too. Hail is hard on every material, and wind lifts any shingle that wasn't nailed right. Tell us what matters most (price, years, looks or hail) and we'll tell you which roof fits.

sections.heading: A Crew That Cleans Up
body: Tearing a roof off throws nails, shingle scraps and grit everywhere. How a crew handles that says a lot about the crew.
When the last shingle is on, the crew walks the yard, the beds and the driveway and picks up what came off the roof. That walk is part of the job, not an extra.
Anthony then comes back to check on the roof. A roof is a big purchase, and we'd rather hear your question now than have you wondering about it later.

sections.heading: What Decides the Price
body: Every roof quote is built from the same few things. Understanding them helps you compare quotes fairly.
tail: We give you a detailed estimate after we've seen the roof. A number given over the phone, before anyone has looked, is a guess.

items.title: Size and pitch
items.text: More squares of roof means more material and labor. A steep roof is slower and costlier to work on safely.

items.title: Material
items.text: Composition shingles, metal and tile run at very different prices. Shingles cost the least up front; metal and tile cost more and last longer.

items.title: Decking repair
items.text: Rotted wood can only be found once the old roof is off. A good estimate explains how that's handled before the work starts.

items.title: Layers and details
items.text: Old layers to tear off, chimneys, skylights and valleys all add labor. A simple, single-layer roof costs less to replace than a cut-up one.

sections.heading: Insurance and Storm Damage

Our part is the roof. We can tell you what the damage is and what it will take to fix it, and that's the information the adjuster works from. We can't tell you what your insurer will decide.

A small repair done now is a small bill. The same leak left through a wet spring becomes rotted wood, stained drywall and sometimes mold.
If you can see daylight, a hole or a missing section, call as soon as we're open, and keep the water off your belongings in the meantime. We'd rather get to a leak early than late.

sections.heading: What Usually Needs Repairing
body: Most roof leaks are not a worn-out roof. We trace most of them to a short list of small places:
tail: Each of these costs far less to fix than a roof. The trick is finding which one it is.

items.title: Flashing
items.text: The metal around chimneys, walls and skylights bends, rusts or pulls loose. Water slips behind it and runs down inside the wall or onto the ceiling.

items.title: Vent boots
items.text: The rubber collars around plumbing pipes crack in the sun years before the shingles do. Replacing one is a short job.

items.title: Chimney chases and caps
items.text: The framed box around a chimney leaks at its joints and where its siding meets the roof. The stain shows up inside and looks like a roof leak.

items.title: Missing or lifted shingles
items.text: Wind breaks the seal on a shingle and rips it off the next time it blows. The felt underneath can't keep out rain for long.

items.title: Valleys
items.text: Where two slopes meet, all the water runs through one narrow channel. Worn or badly cut valleys are a common leak point.

sections.heading: Wind and Storm Damage
body: Wind in Kansas doesn't just take shingles off, it creases them. A shingle can look fine from the yard and still have a broken seal, ready to go the next time the wind comes up.
Hail leaves bruises and bare spots that you can't see from the ground, and they leak a year later. After a bad storm, it's worth having someone on the roof even if nothing looks wrong.
We repair storm-damaged roofs, from a few shingles to the larger jobs. If the damage is spread across much of the roof, we'll say so plainly, because that's a different decision.

sections.quote: My roof got really messed up by a bad wind and River City Roofing made it super quick and easy to get it fixed. Anthony was very friendly and easy to work with and the guys on the crew really worked their tails off to get my roof done quickly!
sections.name: Jordan S.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a Leak
body: Call (316) 295-2159 and tell us where the water shows up, when it started and whether a storm came first. We set a time to come look.
Someone from River City checks the attic, then the roof, and finds the opening. You get a detailed estimate for the repair that stops it before we start.

sections.heading: How We Find the Leak
body: Your own clues help: whether the stain grows in every rain or only when wind drives it sideways, and whether it sits near a chimney, a bathroom fan or a plumbing vent. They narrow it down, but they don't settle it, because water rarely drips straight down from the opening.
So we start in the attic, where a leak leaves dark streaks, wet insulation and damp wood. Then we go up on the roof and follow the trail to the opening.

Sometimes the trail ends somewhere other than the shingles. That's the whole point of looking: you pay to fix what's actually letting water in. You get a detailed estimate for the repair that stops it.

sections.quote: We had a leak in the kitchen ceiling. We assumed it was from the roof so we called a slew of different contractors. We ended up going with River City Roofing as Anthony crawled into the attic and onto the roof and found that our CHIMNEY CHASE was leaking.
sections.name: Brant C.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: We'd rather fix a roof that can be fixed. If most of the roof is sound and the damage is in one place, repair is the right answer.
Here's when we'll tell you it's time to stop repairing:
tail: In that case the next step is a [roof replacement](/roof-replacement-wichita-ks/), and we'll show you why. If it's a repair, we'll say that too.

items.title: Shingles curling, cracking or bare across the whole slope
items.text: The roof is worn out, not damaged in one spot. A patch holds a season, not years.

items.title: Repaired several times and still leaking
items.text: New leaks keep opening in old shingles. The repairs start to add up to the price of a roof.

items.title: Soft or sagging decking
items.text: If more than a small spot of wood is soft, water has been getting in for a while. That wood has to be replaced, and so does the roof over it.

items.title: Granules collecting in your gutters
items.text: Shingles shed their grit as they age. A lot of it in the gutters means the surface protecting them is nearly gone.

sections.heading: What Affects the Price of a Repair
body: Repair prices vary because repairs vary. Resealing a vent boot is a short job. Rebuilding a chimney chase or replacing a section of rotted decking is not.
Roof pitch, height and access change the time it takes. Wet weather can delay work. The kind of shingle matters, since older styles can be hard to match.
We give you a detailed estimate once we've found the problem, so you know what you're paying for before we start.

sections.heading: Storm Damage and Your Insurance
body: If wind or hail did the damage, your homeowner's policy may cover some or all of the repair. That depends on your policy, your deductible and what the adjuster decides.
Take photos of the damage and the date of the storm, and keep any receipts for temporary fixes. We can't promise how your insurer will respond, but we can tell you exactly what's wrong with the roof.
